clue.text: Change colour visibly from goitre — pain throbbing

explanation.surface: A medical oddity: a swelling in the neck that pulses so hard it seems to change colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The goitre is pure scenery: the answer runs across the end of 'goitre', all of 'pain' and the start of 'throbbing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a fresh coat in a different shade is to change its colour.

clue.text: About time, vessel determines to go back

parts.note: re is Latin for 'concerning', used as 'about'
an urn is a vessel, such as one for ashes or tea

explanation.surface: A ship's crew, running short of time, resolves to head home.
explanation.definitionFit: To return is simply to come or go back to where one started.

clue.text: At no time taken in by blow to belly

parts.note: a punch is a blow

explanation.walkthrough: 'At no time' reads as 'never', but 'no' is a deletion indicator acting on 'At' and 'time'.

clue.text: Cruelly using Indian's skin over colour, chiefly, they say

explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' is the sound signal: 'hue mainly' is heard, and 'over' places the skin of Indian above it.

clue.text: Work fulfilled? About time

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
met as in 'met the target', fulfilled

explanation.surface: A worker asks if the job is done at last, and is told it's about time.

explanation.definitionFit: In music, the pace or speed of a piece is its time.

clue.text: Tramps given clothes — about time

explanation.surface: Vagrants are finally handed something to wear, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: TOERAG is British slang for a scruffy, contemptible person, originally a tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: Toerags were vagrants who wrapped rags round their feet, so worthless people or down-and-outs.

clue.text: Scourge of people between rock and hard place

a tor, a craggy rock, is also a hard place

clue.text: Throw out — time's up

parts.note: the word time, with 's for is linking it to the indicator

explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge, such as light, heat or sound.

clue.text: Acceptance of taking our time over choice

parts.note: AD, anno domini, is the era we live in

explanation.surface: A deliberate decision to take one's time before choosing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of taking' links the definition to the wordplay.

clue.text: For poet, at no time stopping chorus of contempt

clue.text: This is reality: being ruthless to make time

explanation.walkthrough: 'ruthless' is read as 'without RUTH': the answer less RUTH leaves T, for time.
explanation.definitionFit: The truth is what is actually so, the real state of things.

clue.text: Composer working in orchestral movies cut lavish set pieces

cut means some letters are removed from the rearranged pool

clue.text: Note what 10, 13 and 22 did: restored calm

Morricone, Coward and Domino each composed music

explanation.surface: A footnote saying the three composers restored a sense of calm.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose oneself again after being upset is to regain one's composure, settling down.

clue.text: Boatman goes on south to get sun?

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
a tar is a sailor, a man of boats; the setter's pseudonym too

clue.text: Composer of old, once with movement about conflict

the letters move about into a new order

parts.note: war is a conflict

clue.text: Boatman taken in, new to love and so on — about time

love is zero in tennis, O
taken as written
the setter calls himself one

clue.text: Besotted with clue to stun

explanation.surface: Someone so infatuated that a single hint knocks them out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being crazy about someone means infatuated, smitten.

clue.text: Johnson returns with nothing in bungled alert — about time

nothing is zero, O

clue.text: Retired at fun run — lead didn't cut the odds

clue.text: Not really at all queer, I figure that's the same on all sides

indicators.note: the letters are not really in this order; they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protesting that they're not at all odd, just regular all round.

clue.text: Terrible about time, to be frank

parts.note: dire means terrible
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone admitting, to be honest, that they're dreadful at timekeeping.

clue.text: Centrally imposed overtime, holder of innumerable letters — one's job

letters as in the letters of the word being picked from

clue.text: Yearn for sleep? About time

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Longing for a snooze, and about time too.

clue.text: Composer of music and player of it: so damn wild

clue.text: Part of tent peg and rod lie around

clue.text: Declare time to head off

clue.text: Liberal, easy, not into enforcing norms toward beginners

indicators.note: beginners means the opening letter of each preceding word is taken

clue.text: Unruly girl, out of time: liability inside bar, British

parts.note: late means having run out of time
